title: Machine end
description: The body of the signed POST /v1/dispatches/<dispatch_id>/machine-end, application/json: the starter reports the result of deleting the machine it created for the dispatch, or that it has no record of a machine for the dispatch. The starter sends the call only for the machine that it created for the dispatch, or, with the state gone, for a dispatch for which it has no record of a machine. For a machine that the starter has, it sends the call after its delete call, the command delete of the machine adapter, https://qory.dev/contracts/machines/v1/delete.schema.json. It repeats the delete call until that call returns gone, and then sends gone. The starter sends gone for every dispatch for which the command make of the machine adapter, https://qory.dev/contracts/machines/v1/make.schema.json, returned a machine, every dispatch whose release was refused 409 machine_exists, release.schema.json, and every dispatch that is the key of a machine in an answer of the command list of the machine adapter, https://qory.dev/contracts/machines/v1/list.schema.json. It sends gone once the dispatch's machine is gone or once the no-record case of the state gone applies. In the no-record case, a successful answer of the command list, received at or after max_lifetime_minutes after the claim, claim-answer.schema.json, contained no machine with the dispatch in key. A failed list call is no proof. A released dispatch may still get gone with no machine; the control plane accepts it with the signed 204. When the dispatch had no earlier machine event and no refusal took its slot again, its slot stays free; otherwise the accepted gone frees the slot, because the release ended the dispatch. From the first machine event of the dispatch, as claim.schema.json defines it, the dispatch keeps the slot it took at the claim at least until the control plane accepts gone for the dispatch. An accepted gone frees the slot once the dispatch has ended or is stale, whether or not dispatched or a machine end with the state deleting came first. Until then, the dispatch keeps the slot, and the slot is freed when the dispatch ends or goes stale. Before the first machine event, the release, the lapse of the lease or the end of the dispatch frees the slot, as claim.schema.json describes. An accepted machine end other than gone takes a freed slot again, even when the node pool is then over its instance limit; the dispatch then keeps it at least until the control plane accepts gone. Such a machine end still gets the signed 204. An accepted gone never takes a slot, and after an accepted gone no call takes the slot again. Even when no gone arrives, the control plane frees the slot under the time limit for a slot, claim.schema.json. That limit is max_lifetime_minutes plus 60 minutes after the latest of the claim, the first accepted dispatched, the first accepted redemption of the run code, the last accepted machine end, and the last refusal that took the slot again. A dispatched or a redemption sent again does not move the time limit, because only the first accepted one counts. The starter has no limit on machines other than the node pool's instance limit. The states deleting and delete_failed are optional. The call may come any number of times, before or after the dispatch ends. Each send is built anew, with a later time and a new signature, as https://qory.dev/contracts/integration/v1/definitions.schema.json describes for a request sent again, so the replay rule does not refuse it. The starter sends one call at a time for a dispatch: it sends the next only after the answer to the one before, or after it gave that one up. The control plane applies the calls in the order it receives them and compares no time, and every accepted call replaces the state, so delete_failed can be followed by deleting. The state gone is final: a later call changes nothing and still gets the 204. A gone after the time limit for a slot freed the slot also gets the signed 204. A dispatch_id that is unknown, or of another node pool than the key's, is refused 403 forbidden, with the same signed body either way, so nobody learns whether an id exists. The signature with the pool's access key and that check authorise the request, not the id. A signed 400, 403 or 404 refusal ends the starter's attempts to send this call for the dispatch, because the same call sent again cannot succeed; the delete calls go on. After any other failure to send gone, an unsigned answer among them, the starter keeps sending gone, each send built anew, until the control plane accepts it with the signed 204. After any other failure to send deleting or delete_failed, the starter may send that state again for a limited time, and then drops it. A machine end is refused for the first of these that applies, in this order: 403 forbidden, as above; 503 unavailable, the control plane cannot store the call at that moment, and the starter sends it again later, built anew, as above for each state. It is never refused 410 gone or 409 lease_expired, because a machine usually ends after its dispatch. On success the control plane answers a signed 204 with no body. The request is signed with the pool's access key as definitions.schema.json describes. The control plane refuses a time more than 300 seconds from its clock, either way, or a request whose signature it has already seen, with an unsigned 401. A member this schema does not define is refused, invalid_request.

version.description: The document format. The control plane refuses a version it does not read.

time.description: When the starter built the body, RFC 3339 in UTC with whole seconds. The control plane refuses a time more than 300 seconds from its clock, either way, with an unsigned 401.

state.description: The result of deleting the machine. deleting: the starter's delete call was accepted, and the machine may still exist. gone: the machine adapter's delete call returned that no machine with the id exists at the vendor, https://qory.dev/contracts/machines/v1/delete-answer.schema.json, or, in the no-record case, the starter has no record of a machine for the dispatch: a successful answer of the command list of the machine adapter, https://qory.dev/contracts/machines/v1/list.schema.json, received at or after max_lifetime_minutes after the claim, claim-answer.schema.json, contained no machine with the dispatch in key. A failed list call is no proof. For a machine whose id the starter has, a missing entry in a list is no proof that the machine is gone, because a vendor's list can lag. delete_failed: the delete call failed, and the starter treats the machine as still existing.
